name: opsworks-cm
description: AWS OpsWorks CM AWS OpsWorks for configuration management (CM) is a service that runs and manages configuration management servers.

subcommands.name: create-server
subcommands.description: Creates and immedately starts a new server. The server is ready to use when it is in the HEALTHY state. By default, you can create a maximum of 10 servers.

options.name: --associate-public-ip-address
options.description: Associate a public IP address with a server that you are launching. Valid values are true or false. The default value is true

options.name: --no-associate-public-ip-address
options.description: Associate a public IP address with a server that you are launching. Valid values are true or false. The default value is true

options.name: --custom-domain
options.description: An optional public endpoint of a server, such as https://aws.my-company.com.

options.name: --custom-certificate
options.description: A PEM-formatted HTTPS certificate. The value can be be a single, self-signed certificate, or a certificate chain.

options.name: --custom-private-key
options.description: A private key in PEM format for connecting to the server by using HTTPS.

options.name: --disable-automated-backup
options.description: Enable or disable scheduled backups. Valid values are true or false. The default value is true

options.name: --no-disable-automated-backup
options.description: Enable or disable scheduled backups. Valid values are true or false. The default value is true

options.name: --engine
options.description: The configuration management engine to use. Valid values include ChefAutomate and Puppet

options.name: --engine-model
options.description: The engine model of the server. Valid values in this release include Monolithic for Puppet and Single for Chef

options.name: --engine-version
options.description: The major release version of the engine that you want to use. For a Chef server, the valid value for EngineVersion is currently 2.

options.name: --engine-attributes
options.description: Optional engine attributes on a specified server.

options.name: --backup-retention-count
options.description: The number of automated backups that you want to keep. Whenever a new backup is created, AWS OpsWorks CM deletes the oldest backups if this number is exceeded.

options.name: --server-name
options.description: The name of the server. The server name must be unique within your AWS account, within each region.

options.name: --instance-profile-arn
options.description: The ARN of the instance profile that your Amazon EC2 instances use.

options.name: --instance-type
options.description: The Amazon EC2 instance type to use. For example, m5.large

options.name: --key-pair
options.description: The Amazon EC2 key pair to set for the instance.

options.name: --preferred-maintenance-window
options.description: The start time for a one-hour period each week during which AWS OpsWorks CM performs maintenance on the instance.

options.name: --preferred-backup-window
options.description: The start time for a one-hour period during which AWS OpsWorks CM backs up application-level data on your server if automated backups are enabled.

options.name: --security-group-ids
options.description: A list of security group IDs to attach to the Amazon EC2 instance.

options.name: --service-role-arn
options.description: The service role that the AWS OpsWorks CM service backend uses to work with your account.

options.name: --subnet-ids
options.description: The IDs of subnets in which to launch the server EC2 instance.   Amazon EC2-Classic customers: This field is required. All servers must run within a VPC.

options.name: --tags
options.description: A map that contains tag keys and tag values to attach to an AWS OpsWorks for Chef Automate or AWS OpsWorks for Puppet Enterprise server.

options.name: --backup-id
options.description: If you specify this field, AWS OpsWorks CM creates the server by using the backup represented by BackupId

options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.
